newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-HOGAN A WORLD BEATER IN MODERN TIMES - PLAYER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HOGAN A WORLD BEATER IN MODERN TIMES - PLAYER.

text.p: Ben Hogan would have been "a world beater" had he played today, Gary Player said on Friday.
"Had Ben played with all the modern-day equipment pros have now and I suspect he would be right up there," said Player, winner of nine majors.
Hogan, who collected 63 PGA Tour victories during an illustrious career, died on Friday. He was 84.
Player, competing in a PGA Seniors tournament at Royal Portrush in Northern Ireland, said: "Ben had a wonderful career playing with inferior equipment and little prize money.
"Who else but Ben would have been able to win a British Open, a U.S. Masters and a U.S.Open in the same year (1953)?

"And the remarkable thing about that was that he didn't make the grand slam that year because he couldn't play the U.S. PGA. In those days because of transport the way it was he didn't get back to do so. "He was one of the hardest workers I've ever known in my life, dedicating himself solely to golf...He was always a credit to the professional game.
"I have never seen three players like Ben, Sam Snead and Byron Nelson. Given the conditions nowadays they would still be world beaters."
